ai.description: This caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark brown to slate-grey with a paler venter. Key features include a distinct tail, 100–115 primary annuli, and a terminal shield. Family: Ichthyophiidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus bombayensis* is best distinguished by its distinctively pointed snout and the presence of a clear, visible eye socket, which is absent in many other caecilians.
ai.habitat: The Bombay Caecilian inhabits moist, leaf-littered soils within tropical evergreen forests and plantations along the Western Ghats, typically at elevations of 200–1,000m.
ai.behavior: The Bombay Caecilian is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through moist soil to forage for earthworms and other small subterranean invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Bombay Caecilian is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females guarding their eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus bombayensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka at moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Bombay Caecilian does not produce an advertisement call, as this species lacks a vocal apparatus and relies on tactile and chemical cues for communication.
